coverageSpotVerification.detail: I read every mapped test end to end (scripts/acceptance.mjs for M1 and scripts/test-m{2,3,4,5,6,8}.mjs) and checked each sampled mapping against its assertion's observable. Every suite-required assertion in M1–M6 and M8 appears in the manifest with the right count (M1 7, M2 22, M3 7, M4 5, M5 6, M6 5, M8 6) and each mapped test really exercises that observable — m6-a13 for instance replays the 50-action sample and then verifies every post, message, reaction, follow, like, repost and membership against the log rather than trusting the adapter's own return. Re-running the suites regenerated a byte-identical assertion→test mapping, so the manifest is produced mechanically from the tests rather than hand-written. Two mappings are weaker than their assertion text without being dishonest: m2-a22/a23 drive pagination through the sentinel "Load more" control rather than a scroll gesture (infinite scroll does exist and I verified it independently — scrolling alone took the feed from 20 to 72/80 items), and m2-a13 proxies "no preview card" by the absence of an iframe (I checked iframes, videos and image count instead). m3-a10/a11 are honestly mapped to a test that genuinely drives the quoted-reply UI, but that test fails deterministically in my environment for the race described in defect d-04 — a suite-reliability problem, not a mapping-honesty problem. No milestone is adjudicated capability-failure.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("M1–M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap") and the 90 anchor ("every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts"), close to but short of 90.
O1.justification: Full-run scope is M1–M8. M1–M6 and M8 are green and every one of their 110 assertions passed my independent execution (suite + API + browser automation + choreography receipts): 13/13 M1, 27/27 M2, 15/15 M3, 12/12 M4, 12/12 M5, 13/13 M6, 18/18 M8. That is far past the 60 anchor — M5, M6 and M8 are not patchy, they are complete, including the shortened-window expiry behaviour, the scheduled digest with its authorization rule, and the native cold-offline proof. Two things hold it under 90. First, M7 was never attempted (record status not-run; no poll entity, vote path or message-count surface exists in the lane), so 9 of the 119 in-scope assertions score not passed and one of eight milestones contributes nothing — the 90 anchor requires every in-scope milestone green. Second, the 90 anchor names platform-proof artifacts explicitly, and the native artifacts, while real and passing, do not meet the frozen artifact set in choreography/simulator.md (no uninterrupted screen recording bound to the accepted runs, no receipts.schema.json-conformant m6-ios-receipts.jsonl, no run manifest with SHA-256 digests). 110/119 assertions and 7/8 milestones, with that artifact-form gap, place this at 82.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("a few medium defects off the happy path") and the 90 anchor ("only cosmetic nits"), nearer 60 because one defect is a correctness violation of a pinned invariant rather than a nit.
O2.justification: Eleven defects beyond the checklist: one major, eight minor, two cosmetic. The major one (d-01) is a real correctness bug on an explicitly pinned invariant — the group aggregate receipt goes read → sent when a removed member is re-added, because the aggregate recomputes min(receipt state) over currently-active members instead of the send-time recipient set with drop-outs removed; the sequence sent → sent → read → sent is reproducible and reachable through the ordinary admin remove/re-add flow the harness itself drives. Against that: I found no crash, no data loss, no ordering error, and no authorization hole. Twenty-six of my twenty-seven adversarial trust-boundary probes were correctly denied server-side (cross-user DM history/metadata/send, non-member reaction, cross-user edit/delete, non-member and anonymous asset fetch, removed-member read and write, non-admin add/promote, handle takeover, access and refresh tokens after logout, anon and signed-in-user PostgREST reads and RPC on every clqfa_ table and function); the twenty-seventh (d-02/d-03) is a latent exposure that currently fails closed. The remaining minors are a deterministically failing assertion in the lane's own M3 suite (d-04), a flaky M4 suite wait (d-06), one plaintext fixture password in a retained XCTest log (d-05), a misleading documented field (d-07), a fixed ~2.3 req/s idle polling cost with a full cached-history rewrite per tick (d-08), and two unbounded in-process maps (d-09). That is more than cosmetic nits but well short of multiple high-severity defects in core flows.

O4.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush") and the 90 anchor ("reads, ordered queued writes, receipt transitions, and offline search all behave as specced on the native proof — on full runs including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence"); the demonstrated behaviour is at 90, the artifact form is not.
O4.justification: Scored from the choreography and simulator artifacts only. The behavioural content of the 90 anchor is all present and mechanically asserted, not claimed: XCTest CliqueOfflineTests.testColdOfflineMediaAndSearch (TEST SUCCEEDED, real simulator UDID 87E00D66…, 7 checkpoint screenshots) cold-launches the app with the recorded backend process stopped and asserts cached history renders, a previously viewed photo opens in the viewer, the cached video player clock advances past 1.0 s, the previously opened view-once message reports value "opened" with its control disabled and no viewer node, and a cold-offline prefix search returns the named token through the app's own Search action; testDurableOfflineRestart asserts two offline composes render pending, survive app termination and relaunch while still offline, then flush exactly once in order and reach "read", with an independent read through Bob's session (evidence/native-queue-api-verification.json) counting exactly two ordered writes. M8's multi-device evidence is separately green in the web choreography receipts (m8-a13 cross-device live 2897 ms, m8-a14 cross-device read-state clear 2085 ms, m8-a15 dual-offline convergence with both flushes, m8-a16 receipts advancing), and the web carrier's own queue segment passed (flushMs 2851). Three things keep it below 90, all about evidence rather than behaviour: choreography/simulator.md requires a qualifying native run to produce an uninterrupted screen recording, an m6-ios-receipts.jsonl validated against receipts.schema.json, and an m6-ios-run.json manifest with SHA-256 digests of both, and states that a recording without structured receipts is not a pass and receipts without the bound recording and manifest are not a pass — the accepted runs (m6-native-media-proof-retry2, m8-native-proof-retry5) carry only PNG screenshots plus a lane-authored summary JSON; screen recordings exist only in earlier failed attempts. The M6 cold-offline sequence and the queued-write/flush sequence were also demonstrated in two separate XCTest runs rather than one continuous session as simulator.md steps 2–7 specify. Both gaps are disclosed honestly (m6-native-proof.json says the queue evidence is "separately evidenced in M8 proof" and states that offline is a stopped backend rather than a device network cut, which simulator.md permits; simulator-status.json distinguishes actual native evidence from Hermes exports), and O4 explicitly weighs the honesty of a claim/guarantee gap — which is why this lands at 78 rather than lower.

O5.bandRationale: First-match band evaluation in the order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Band 0 does not fire: I checked the retained end-state receipts against the committed instrument/fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json and all 18 expected entity counts plus followEdgeCount match exactly at the final checkpoint (users 1008, posts 50228, messages 100015, quotedReplies 2736, activeReactions 2000, disappearingSettingsEnabled 0), the 10% and 50% checkpoint receipts match their checkpoint manifests, the lane verifier asserts the per-user, per-chat, per-group maps and the named O5 fixtures with deepEqual against that committed manifest, receipt accounting is complete (167157 actions / 167157 receipts) and scale.log's sha256 matches the fixture digest; the replay wall cap is uncalibrated in this instrument version (record capSeconds null) and capExhausted is false. Band 30 then fires: two frozen degradation rules fail in the retained probe record. Global message search mid-curve — p95 300.1 ms at 10%, 382.3 ms at 50%, 364.7 ms at 100%, so the 50% point sits above the 328.8 ms line between the endpoints. Insights mid-curve — 635.1 ms at 10%, 2472.1 ms at 50%, 661.9 ms at 100%, against a 647.0 ms interpolated line, a 3.8x overshoot. I recomputed both from the raw checkpoint samples rather than taking the lane's pass/fail flags. Caveat recorded because it matters for reading the number, not for the band: the 50% checkpoint looks environmentally contaminated — following-u0901 measured 3567 ms at 50% against ~300 ms at both 10% and 100%, and several probes were faster at 100% than at 10%, which no genuine superlinear curve produces — and three frozen rules (celebrity write comparison, group send-to-render responsiveness, native cold-sync memory bound) were never measured at all, so they cannot be credited as passing either. The frozen band function has no noise tolerance and the grader is instructed to apply it exactly. Re-measurement was impossible: the brief requires the lane to delete all owned hosted state after the final report, and evidence/cleanup.json records both scale schemas dropped, so the 100k-message corpus no longer exists.

notes: DEVIATIONS FROM THE FROZEN PROTOCOL (N=1 calibration run, not claim-eligible). (1) No holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped, wave.probeSetSha256 is the sentinel "none-uncommitted", and probeResults is empty. No probes were invented. Because applicability.json scopes O3 to "the wave's secret rotated holdout probes only", O3 records null even though its predicate (M6 green plus M1–M5 attempted) is satisfied — the only permitted input does not exist. My own 27 trust-boundary probes are recorded in the trace and scored under O2, never as O3. (2) The claude family has not passed the grader calibration gate, so calibrationPassed is false and this grade is labelled uncalibrated-grader; sameFamilyGraded is false (the builder was gpt-6-astra, a different family). (3) Timing-sensitive checks are judged best-of-3 with host load recorded beside each measurement in the trace; this machine is shared and load averages ranged from 7.8/27.6/69.7 at session start to 9.2/14.2/20.9 mid-session.
